details.prompt: 请以当前研究方案为依据绘制基金技术路线图。逐项对齐科学问题、研究内容、数据、方法、验证和产物，沿用已确认的框架。未提供的方法或样本量不添加；交付原生可编辑PPT或SVG、预览和原文对照表，检查时间线、字体、连线与文字溢出。

选择矢量或图像生成方式
核对事实文字和期刊要求
details.prompt: 请为这篇论文制作图形摘要，先提炼研究对象、核心方法、主要发现和适用边界，建立事实与图形对应表。按我指定方式制作；AI插图不得重造统计图、病理证据或数值。交付源文件或提示词、预览、事实核对表，并说明可编辑范围。

details.description: 将科研论文转为有证据主线的中文汇报PPT，保留关键原图、出处和逐页讲稿，交付真实PPTX。
inputs: 论文全文、补充材料或完整笔记
听众与汇报时长
模板和必须讲解的图
workflow: 按论文类型确定叙事
建立问题到证据的主线
完整提取关键图与图注
写讲稿并逐页检查
details.prompt: 请把这篇论文制作成中文文献汇报PPT。先判断属于临床、方法、资源、机制还是综述研究，建立问题—设计—主要证据—局限的主线。每页一个主要判断，保留原图坐标、图例与出处；交付真实PPTX、逐页讲稿、术语表和渲染检查报告，不虚构论文未报告的内容。

答辩阶段、时长和学校模板
完成情况与实际结果
outputs: 讲稿、备份页和问题清单
workflow: 确定汇报阶段与时间
映射总问题与子研究
选择能支持结论的证据
准备讲稿和答辩备份
details.prompt: 请依据当前论文/方案制作开题、中期或答辩PPT，先确认汇报阶段。用总科学问题串联子研究，逐项对应理论、数据、方法、结果或计划；已完成、进行中和拟开展明确区分。交付可编辑PPTX、讲稿、备份页与检查报告，数字和技术路线以当前文件为准。

details.name: 统一视觉的图片型PPT
details.description: 在用户接受整页图片的前提下制作视觉统一的图片型PPT，保留原图、提示词和讲稿，明确对象不可单独编辑。

workflow: 确认图片页符合使用需求
制定统一视觉并做代表页
生成其余页面并核查文字
组装PPT并保留来源
details.prompt: 请把这份材料制作成视觉统一的图片型PPT，我接受整页图片不能逐元素编辑。先确定逐页信息与视觉风格，制作代表页；采用同一风格完成全套，准确保留事实和必要原图。交付PPTX、逐页高清图、提示词、讲稿和检查说明。

details.name: 科研教学、方法科普与分镜PPT
details.description: 把研究方法或科研知识组织成教学幻灯片、图解卡片和视频分镜，保留准确术语、来源与受众层次。

从问题到例子解释方法
将图解与讲述对应

details.prompt: 请将这个研究方法做成教学PPT与分镜。先设定听众需要掌握的能力，再按问题、直观解释、例子、操作、误区组织；公式和例子保留正确口径。区分真实研究与教学示意，提供逐页口播、图解、来源和导出检查。

details.name: 科研图与PPT质量检查
details.description: 检查科研图和PPT的证据、图文一致、对象编辑、字体、裁切和导出，区分自动结构检查与人工视觉检查。
inputs: 源文件与最终导出文件
原文/原始数据和图源
目标格式、尺寸与模板
outputs: 按严重度排序的问题清单
结构检查和视觉检查状态
workflow: 核对来源与事实
检查文件结构和可编辑性
按最终尺寸查看每页

details.prompt: 请审核这些科研图/PPT。核对数字、单位、方法、图号与原文一致，再检查字体、上下标、文字溢出、图像裁切、连接线及可编辑范围。结构检查与视觉检查分别报告；按严重度列问题并修复可直接修复项，不把脚本通过等同于版式完美。

records.collection_title: 政策主题与研究逻辑
records.title: ☂️ 长期护理保险

details.title: ☂️ 长期护理保险
details.definition: 针对失能照护需求的社会保险安排；参保、失能评估、符合待遇资格与实际获得服务须分开。2026建制阶段应与此前试点版本区分。
details.logic: 筹资与统筹 → 失能评估 → 待遇支付 → 正式照护供给 → 家庭照护与健康/经济结果
clauses: 参保范围、缴费主体与筹资结构
等级、持续失能、评估机构与复评申诉
居家/社区/机构待遇和服务项目
等待、限额、定点、支付与监管
variables: 地区×版本×不同实施日期
政策前功能/失能与认知
服务可得性、实际利用和家庭照护时间
自付、家庭劳动与健康结果
questions: 保障扩展能否缓解照护者负担？
同等失能下，城乡或不同参保类型的服务可及性是否不同？
支付激励是否改变居家与机构护理的组合？
methods: 条款比较与政策工具分析
交错DID/事件研究（实际实施时点）
混合方法与实施/公平评价
pitfalls: 用试点名单年份替代待遇支付日期
把所有老年人当待遇合格者
将地方比例写成全国统一标准
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

records.collection_title: 政策主题与研究逻辑
records.title: 🏡 家庭病床

details.title: 🏡 家庭病床
details.definition: 由医疗机构评估并在符合条件患者居住场所提供连续医疗服务，有建床、责任团队、病历与撤床等要求；不等于所有上门服务。
details.logic: 申请与评估 → 协议/建床 → 连续服务与监测 → 转诊/撤床 → 结算与质量
clauses: 对象、疾病状态、就医困难与场所条件
机构许可、服务能力与人员资质
建撤床、首次访视、频次与医疗记录
服务价格、医保范围和结算
与家庭医生、养老机构、长护险的衔接
variables: 机构开办/个人建床日期、床日与访视
功能、病情、照护支持与距离
住院急诊、安全事件、体验与自付
医护工时、交通和社会总成本
questions: 能否提高行动不便患者的连续医疗可及性？
是否替代部分住院，同时保障安全和体验？
支付与服务半径如何影响供给？
methods: 政策内容—执行过程联合分析
pitfalls: 把一次护理等同建床
只看住院减少而忽略选择与安全
将上海职工医保比例外推其他人群和地区
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

records.collection_title: 政策主题与研究逻辑
records.title: 🚪 老年人居家医疗

details.title: 🚪 老年人居家医疗
details.definition: 把适宜医疗服务延伸到居住场所的供给安排，可由不同服务形式实现；需区分服务内容、连续性与资格。
details.logic: 就医障碍 → 机构供给与上门能力 → 服务触达 → 连续性与患者负担
variables: 功能、居住、距离与家庭支持
服务项目/频次与等待
交通、自付和未满足需求
questions: 哪些人有需要却未获得服务？
供给扩展是否改善弱势人群可及性？
methods: 两部/计数模型与公平分析
pitfalls: 居家场所不等于居家养老
“支持开展”不等于实际提供或医保报销
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

records.title: 📱 互联网+护理服务

details.title: 📱 互联网+护理服务
details.definition: 依托信息平台连接申请与线下护理供给；分析平台、实体机构与护士的责任，以及安全和支付。
details.logic: 线上申请 → 需求/风险评估 → 机构派出 → 线下护理 → 记录与反馈
clauses: 项目准入、人员资质、知情同意
variables: 平台上线、服务地区/项目
订单、完成、取消、时间与严重错误
数字使用能力、价格与需求
questions: 数字渠道能否帮助高需求者，也可能排除哪些人？
methods: 平台分期实施的政策设计
pitfalls: 把平台注册量当完成服务量
把服务价格存在等同已获医保支付

details.definition: 长期服务关系与履约机制，评价应从签约数量走到实际服务、连续性和居民感受。

clauses: 服务包与履约、转诊和信息
variables: 签约、履约、接触频次与连续性
慢病过程指标与患者体验

questions: 签约覆盖扩大是否转成实际履约？
哪些服务安排改善感受与连续性？
methods: 多层模型/合适的政策因果设计
pitfalls: 签约率等同履约率
用满意度替代临床或公平结局
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

clauses: 医疗质量与养老服务衔接
感染、安全、信息和支付责任

records.title: 🧾 DRG按病组付费

details.title: 🧾 DRG按病组付费
details.definition: 按疾病诊断相关分组组织医保支付的安排。分组方案、支付标准、预算、实际结算与例外机制需要分别提取。
details.logic: 预算与分组 → 支付激励 → 医院行为 → 费用/质量/患者选择
clauses: 特例单议、清算与质量约束
variables: 首次实际结算和版本切换
病例组合、编码与严重度
费用、自付、住院日、再入院与质量
questions: 控费是否伴随质量或患者选择变化？
methods: 病例组合调整和异质性
pitfalls: 分组升级等同首次改革
只看均次费用而忽略编码与病例结构
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

records.title: 🔢 DIP按病种分值付费

details.title: 🔢 DIP按病种分值付费
details.definition: 在预算与病种分值等规则下进行医保支付；需区分病种库、分值、点值形成和机构结算。
details.logic: 区域预算 → 病种分值/点值 → 机构策略 → 资源与质量结果
variables: 统筹区实际运行日期与规则
病例组合、编码、机构负荷
费用转移、质量与效率
questions: 预算约束如何影响机构间竞争和服务组合？
pitfalls: 将名义点值当全年最终结算点值
混用医院和统筹区赋值层级
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

records.title: 💊 门诊共济保障

details.title: 💊 门诊共济保障
details.definition: 职工医保门诊保障与个人账户调整等配套改革；应把待遇变化、账户变化和基层支付激励分别测量。
details.logic: 门诊待遇/账户调整 → 就医与购药激励 → 门住院利用 → 负担与公平
clauses: 门诊统筹、起付、比例、限额
variables: 地区/人群生效日期与待遇变化
门诊药店住院利用与自付
年龄、退休和医保身份
questions: 门诊保障扩展是否改变住院替代与费用负担？
pitfalls: 家庭账户共济等于统筹待遇提高
不区分退休与在职待遇或过渡
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

records.title: 🛟 重特大疾病医疗保险与救助

details.title: 🛟 重特大疾病医疗保险与救助
details.definition: 基本医保、大病保险与医疗救助的衔接安排，关注经济困难群体的托底与因病致贫风险。
details.logic: 身份认定 → 多层保障衔接 → 实际自付 → 灾难性支出与福利
variables: 救助资格、实际获得与时间
总费用、报销后自付、家庭资源
灾难性卫生支出阈值/分母
questions: 获得保障者是否仍存在未满足医疗需求？
methods: 公平/财务保护与因果设计
pitfalls: 把大病保险和医疗救助当同一制度
灾难性支出分母前后不一致
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

details.title: 🔗 紧密型县域医共体
details.definition: 县乡村医疗卫生体系的整合安排，重点看管理、资源、服务、医防和激励是否形成实际协同。
details.logic: 治理与资源整合 → 基层承接与连续服务 → 分级诊疗 → 县域健康与效率
clauses: 医防融合、医保支付与绩效
variables: 正式组建、运行与各模块启动
资源下沉、转诊和基层利用
服务质量、连续性与费用
questions: 组织整合的哪些环节真正转化为协同？
pitfalls: 挂名成立即完成紧密整合
把同期DRG/DIP和基层供给变化忽略
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

details.title: 🏙️ 紧密型城市医疗集团
details.definition: 城市网格内组织与服务协作的政策安排；试点列名、集团组建与真实运转应分别记时。

clauses: 服务连续性、医防融合和评价
variables: 试点、组建、运行与覆盖范围
成员关系、流程与转诊
网格服务人群、利用与质量
questions: 网格化治理能否缩短跨机构服务断点？
methods: 多城市政策设计与实施研究
pitfalls: 试点名单日期等于实际服务日
与县域医共体直接混成同一处理
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

details.title: 🪜 分级诊疗与双向转诊
details.definition: 通过能力、分工与激励形成合适就医秩序；基层首诊、转诊与慢病连续管理需拆开测量。
details.logic: 基层能力与激励 → 就医选择/转诊 → 连续性与适宜服务 → 可及与效率
variables: 真实政策与服务启动
基层利用、转诊方向与完成
可避免住院、连续性和患者负担
questions: 提高基层利用是否同时改善适宜性与连续性？
methods: 患者流向/多层/政策评价
pitfalls: 基层比例上升自动等于健康改善
只记录转出不记录接收完成
details.note: 条款维度、研究字段与研究问题是分析建议；政策事实以所列国家/地方原文为依据。

details.title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Background The drivers of mortality and their associated risk factors evolve throughout the course of life. Understanding these transitions is essential for effective, equitable, and age-appropriate health interventions. Methods As part of the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023, we examined life expectancy and the probability of death from birth to age 70 years (70q0) from 1990 to 2023 for each Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member state. In addition, we assessed causes of death and risk factor by age and sex across different life stages. Life expectancy was estimated from age-specific mortality rates with standard demographic techniques, and 70q0 from mortality and GBD life tables. Cause-specific mortality was estimated using the Cause of Death Ensemble model, and risk-attributable mortality using the comparative risk assessment framework. Findings In 2023, regional life expectancy was 70·1 years (95% uncertainty interval 69·6-70·7) for males and 76·2 years (75·7-76·7) for females, ranging from 87·5 years (87·3-87·8) for females in Singapore to 62·1 years (60·8-63·5) for males in Myanmar. Correspondingly, all-cause 70q0 was higher for males than for females. Neonatal disorders were the leading cause of mortality among infants younger than 1 year. Road injuries were the primary driver of mortality among males from adolescence through to early adulthood, accounting for 25·0% (17·0-31·0) of total mortality (8230 [5740-10 800] deaths) in males aged 15-19 years, with mortality rates varying from 3·0 per 100 000 population (2·3-3·7) to 49·0 per 100 000 population (25·0-67·1) between countries. Among females, maternal disorders were the leading cause of death in ages 25-34 years. In mid-adulthood, non-communicable diseases such as ischaemic heart disease and stroke emerged as major causes. Tobacco use was the dominant risk factor across most of adulthood in males, whereas high blood pressure was the prevailing risk factor among adult females. Interpretation Although the leading causes of death have converged across countries, the outcomes of these causes remain divergent, reflecting persistent inequalities across the region. These patterns present a strategic opportunity for multilateral action to mobilise collective resources and achieve regional health equity. Funding Gates Foundation.

details.title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Introduction The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) region, established in 1967, constitutes 8·6% of the global population and is one of the fastest-growing economies in the world. 1 However, the region is characterised by stark socioeconomic asymmetries. The Human Development Index ranged from 0·946 in Singapore to 0·606 in Cambodia in 2025, 2 whereas the projected gross domestic product per capita in 2026 ranges from more than US$107 760 in Singapore to US$1520 in Myanmar. 3 The socioeconomic diversity fundamentally defines the region's health landscape. 4 Since 1990, ASEAN has undergone an unevenly paced epidemiological transition, with persistent infectious and maternal and child health burdens in several states alongside rising non-communicable diseases (NCDs) in all. 5 , 6 Disparities in health system capacity have yielded discrepancies in health outcomes. 4 , 7 , 8 Although health inequities related to specific diseases have been explored within the region, 7 , 8 , 9 , 10 no research has systematically examined comparative all-cause mortality profiles and assessed age-sex-specific patterns from birth to adulthood across the entire ASEAN. A life-course approach addresses this gap by linking early-life exposures and structural determinants to later-life health outcomes and disparities. 11 Earlier regional applications were confined to childhood and adolescence or individual countries, without adulthood or cross-country comparison. 12 Because mortality drivers and their risk factors evolve across the life course, 13 , 14 we apply this framework using the latest findings from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 to examine causes of death across all 11 ASEAN member states. This granular, stage-specific analysis identifies age-sex-specific diseases and risk factors driving mortality to inform targeted interventions, promote longevity, and improve health equity across the region. details.text: Methods Overview Leveraging the best available data sources and a systematic analytical modelling approach, GBD 2023 produced geographically and temporally comparable estimates for various demographic and epidemiological metrics, including life expectancy and mortality for 292 causes of death, by age and sex, across 204 countries and territories, and from 1990 to 2023. 15 , 16 In this study, we examined life expectancy and probability of death from birth to age 70 years (70q0) across ASEAN and its member states from 1990 to 2023, and evaluated mortality patterns specific to cause and risk factor by life stages, sex, and location in 2023. Although Timor-Leste acceded to ASEAN only in October, 2025, we included it to provide the most current evidence base for the bloc as presently constituted, supporting forward-looking regional health planning. We defined life stages as: infancy and childhood (birth to age 9 years); 17 adolescence (ages 10–24 years), following the expanded definition proposed by Sawyer and colleagues, 18 which more closely reflects the biological, neurocognitive, and social transitions of this life stage; and adulthood (age 25 years and older). 19 GBD cause and risk factor hierarchy GBD classifies causes and risk factors into four hierarchical levels. Level 1 comprises three categories: communicable, maternal, neonatal, and nutritional diseases; NCDs; and injuries, partitioned into 22 Level 2 clusters and disaggregated further at Levels 3 and 4. Risk factors are similarly organised, from three Level 1 groups (environmental and occupational, behavioural, and metabolic) into 20 Level 2 clusters with further subdivisions. 15 , 20 For the present analysis, we focused on causes of death at Level 3 and risk factors at Level 2. Data sources and processing Data sources are detailed in the appendix (pp 6–13) ; mortality data were gathered from vital registrations, surveys, literature, and census data across ASEAN. details.title: Causes of death across the life course in the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Discussion This study provides a life-course perspective on the drivers of premature mortality across the ASEAN region. Our findings reveal substantial disparities in life expectancy and 70q0, with a life expectancy gap as wide as 20 years between the lowest-performing and highest-performing member states. Throughout the life course, leading mortality drivers showed similar age patterns: neonatal disorders dominate infancy; lower respiratory infections prevail in early childhood and drowning in later childhood to early adolescence; road injuries impose a substantial burden in adolescence and young adulthood, particularly among males; maternal disorders account for a notable share among young females in many ASEAN states; and NCDs, including ischaemic heart disease, stroke, and diabetes, dominate from mid-adulthood onwards. Yet, outcomes diverge markedly; neonatal mortality rates, for instance, differ 40-fold between the highest-performing and lowest-performing countries. These patterns underscore substantial health inequities and differences in health-system capacity, suggesting opportunities for joint regional action. The increase in life expectancy and reduction in 70q0 between 1990 and 2023 reflect remarkable achievements in population health. The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a temporary decline in 2020–21, before life expectancy resumed its upward trajectory. These advancements were accompanied by socioeconomic development, including gross domestic product growth, rising Human Development Index, and expanded universal health coverage. 24 , 25 However, progress remains uneven. In 2024, Singapore's gross domestic product per capita was 65 times that of Myanmar, with government health spending at 21% of public expenditure versus 4% in Myanmar. 26 The divergence is mirrored in health outcomes across the region. On March 1, 2021, Berkeley, CA, USA, implemented the world's first mandatory healthy checkout ordinance (HCO), prohibiting the display of foods high in added sugars and sweetened beverages, including soft drinks (known as soda in the USA) and confectionery (known as candy in the USA), at store checkouts. The HCO was enforceable on Jan 1, 2022. We aimed to evaluate the association of the HCO with sales of soda (sweetened with sugar or non-sugar sweeteners) and candy in the city. Methods In this quasi-experimental study, we analysed Circana retail scanner data (March 3, 2019, to Dec 31, 2023) from 71 stores in Berkeley and three other comparison cities in California, restricted to chains operating in Berkeley. Data were point-of-sale records for selected food and beverage categories, which were aggregated by store and year-quarter for analysis. Primary outcomes were quarterly volume sales of soda and candy overall and by package size, using thresholds based on products commonly sold at checkouts. Using difference-in-differences regressions with store and year-quarter fixed effects, we estimated the association of the HCO with outcomes after its implementation and after it became enforceable. Findings Circana data included 71 (39%) of 183 identified standalone chain locations across the four cities: 19 (20%) of 93 supermarkets, 42 (59%) of 71 drugstores (ie, retail shops that combine a pharmacy with a general convenience store), and ten (53%) of 19 mass merchandisers. The analytical sample comprised more than 9 million product-store-month soda observations (1·0 million in Berkeley) and more than 52 million product-store-month candy observations (5·6 million in Berkeley), aggregated to 1420 store-quarter observations per outcome. After implementation, the estimated difference in mean soda sales was -2478 L per store-quarter (95% CI -5228 to 272; -23·4%), relative to comparison cities. After enforcement, soda sales were -3891 L per store-quarter (-7774 to -7; -39·5%). Estimates indicated reduced sales of large packages of soda after enforcement (-3800 L, -7571 to -30; -42·5%) and varied by store type. Overall candy sales increased after implementation (220 kg per store-quarter, 95% CI 21 to 420; 10·4%); after enforcement, the estimated difference was 156 kg (95% CI -78 to 390; 7·8%), with the 95% CI including the null. Supermarket sales of small packages of candy decreased by 132 kg after implementation (95% CI -212 to -51; -34·9%) and 156 kg after enforcement (-233 to -78; -43·2%). Interpretation Berkeley's mandatory HCO was found to be associated with decreased soda sales but not decreased overall candy sales after its enforcement. Estimates varied by product category, package size, and store type. Mandatory checkout standards can influence purchases, but implementation and enforcement strategies might need tailoring. Funding US National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases and Bloomberg Philanthropies.

details.title: Global, regional, and national prevalence of second-hand smoke and attributable disease burden in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Background Second-hand smoke (SHS) exposure remains a major source of morbidity and mortality among non-smokers. This study presents the first dedicated Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) publication to systematically quantify SHS prevalence and evaluate its effect as a global risk factor across a broader range of outcomes. Methods Using the GBD 2023 comparative risk assessment framework, we estimated SHS exposure prevalence and attributable disease burden across 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2023, stratified by age and sex. Exposure estimates were derived by synthesising population-based surveys and household composition data through spatiotemporal Gaussian process regression. Relative risks for nine health outcomes, now including asthma, were estimated using the Burden of Proof methodology, and applied to calculate attributable deaths and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs). Findings In 2023, an estimated 2·71 billion (95% UI 2·44-3·02) people worldwide were exposed to SHS, including 767 million (687-858) children aged 0-14 years. Age-standardised prevalence was highest in southeast Asia, east Asia, and Oceania (48·4% [44·0-53·4]), with female individuals in some countries experiencing nearly 1·8 times the exposure prevalence of male individuals. Despite a 22·2% (10·6-32·4) decline in global age-standardised prevalence since 1990, this progress has not been sufficient to reduce the absolute number of exposed individuals, which has remained stable globally and has risen sharply in sub-Saharan Africa (98·5% [62·0-144·4] increase) and North Africa and the Middle East (72·1% [47·8-101·8] increase). In 2023, SHS exposure accounted for 1·66 million (1·33-2·07) deaths and 44·8 million (35·8-54·3) DALYs globally. Ischaemic heart disease was the leading contributor to SHS-attributable DALYs (12·0 million [9·31-15·2]) overall, while lower respiratory infections predominated among children (5·16 million [3·48-7·12]). Interpretation We estimated that SHS remains a substantial driver of global health loss, particularly through cardiovascular and paediatric respiratory diseases. Persistent geographical disparities and growing absolute numbers of exposed individuals in several regions underscore the urgent need for accelerated implementation and enforcement of comprehensive tobacco control measures, particularly to protect women and children in both public and domestic environments. Funding Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Gates Foundation.

details.title: Global, regional, and national prevalence of second-hand smoke and attributable disease burden in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Introduction Tobacco use remains a leading contributor to the global burden of disease, accounting for an estimated 8 million deaths in 2023. 1 A substantial part of this burden falls on non-smokers exposed to second-hand smoke (SHS) through mechanisms similar to those of active smoking. SHS combines the sidestream smoke from the burning tip of tobacco products with the smoke exhaled by smokers. 2 The sidestream component, which dominates the air non-smokers breathe, is unfiltered and incompletely combusted, carrying higher per-unit concentrations of the toxic and carcinogenic compounds than mainstream smoke inhaled by the smoker. 3 Through oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and chronic inflammation, these exposures raise the risk of cardiovascular, respiratory, neoplastic, and metabolic disease. 4 , 5 , 6 Children are especially susceptible, owing to developing airways, an immature immune system, and higher minute ventilation per body mass. 7 These adverse health effects have been recognised for decades, and the scientific consensus that no safe level of exposure exists has made SHS a central focus of tobacco control. This priority was formalised by the 2003 WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC), an international public health treaty whose Article 8 calls for smoke-free legislation protecting non-smokers in workplaces, public transport, and indoor public places. Yet, global enforcement and coverage remain inconsistent: approximately 70% of the world's population is not protected by comprehensive smoke-free laws, and domestic settings, where exposure tends to be most prolonged, remain largely unregulated. 8 Research in context Evidence before this study Exposure to second-hand smoke (SHS) is a globally recognised health risk, with no safe level of inhalation. To assess the existing body of evidence on SHS exposure and disease burden, we searched PubMed for articles published from Jan 1, 2010 to Dec 31, 2025, using the terms (“second-hand smoke” OR “environmental smoke”) AND (“prevalence” OR “epidemiology”) AND (“disease burden” OR “mortality” OR “DALYs” OR “YLL” OR “disability-adjusted life-years”) AND (“global” OR “national” OR “regional”).

details.title: Global, regional, and national prevalence of second-hand smoke and attributable disease burden in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Methods Overview As part of GBD 2023, we estimated the burden of disease attributable to SHS exposure from 1990 to 2023 using the comparative risk assessment framework for 204 countries and territories, by age and sex. Exposure was defined as any current exposure to smoke from combustible tobacco products at home or in the workplace; exposure occurring exclusively in other settings (eg, bars, restaurants, public transport, and private vehicles) is not captured. The population at risk was restricted to non-smokers and occasional smokers; all daily smokers were classified as unexposed to avoid overlap with active smoking. The analysis comprised three steps: estimating prevalence of exposure to SHS by age, sex, geography, and time; determining the relative risk (RR) of nine health outcomes associated with SHS exposure; and calculating population-attributable fractions (PAFs) and attributable burden. This study adheres to GATHER ( appendix, pp 16–17 ) 11 and GBD 2023 is registered with the University of Washington Institutional Review Board (study number 9060). Data sources To estimate prevalence of SHS exposure, we combined cross-sectional self-reported workplace exposure and household-level age and sex composition data with GBD 2023 daily smoking prevalence estimates to compute the probability of residing with at least one daily smoker ( appendix pp 6–8 ). Following previous GBD iterations, 12 we assumed that all non-smokers or occasional smokers living with a daily smoker are exposed to SHS within the home. For workplace exposure, we extracted 395 population-based, representative sources (91 new in GBD 2023) covering 119 of 204 countries and territories. For household composition, we incorporated 938 sources (87 new) covering 173 of 204 locations. Geographical coverage and recency are provided in the appendix (pp 19–20) . A complete list of data sources is available through the Global Health Data Exchange . details.title: Global, regional, and national prevalence of second-hand smoke and attributable disease burden in 204 countries and territories, 1990-2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Discussion This study provides updated quantitative insights into the global prevalence, mortality, and disability associated with SHS exposure by age and sex from 1990 to 2023. Over these 33 years, age-standardised prevalence declined from 43·6% (39·9–47·3) to 33·9% (30·5–37·8), a relative reduction of 22·2% (10·6–32·4), yet population growth kept the absolute number of individuals exposed broadly stable. Marked geographical disparities persist, with prevalence approaching 50% in southeast Asia, east Asia, and Oceania. Children and female individuals also remain disproportionately exposed—767 million (687–858) children aged 0–14 years and 1·49 billion (1·35–1·65) female individuals were exposed to SHS in 2023. SHS exposure was associated with ischaemic heart disease, lower respiratory infections, COPD, and other diseases, accounting for 1·66 million (1·33–2·07) deaths, 39·1 million (31·4–48·1) YLLs, 5·73 million (3·83–7·50) YLDs, and 44·8 million (35·8–54·3) DALYs in 2023. The age-standardised DALY rate fell more than twice as fast as exposure prevalence, reflecting concurrent declines in the background rates of the SHS-attributable diseases rather than reduced exposure alone. These findings underscore the persistent gap in protecting non-smokers from the harms of SHS. Reducing population exposure to SHS is a cornerstone of global tobacco control efforts. Progress under Article 8 of the FCTC and the WHO MPOWER framework, whose protect component directly addresses SHS, has been measurable but uneven. 15 As of 2024, 79 countries have achieved the highest standard in the protect measure, with all public places completely smoke-free or at least 90% of the population covered by comprehensive subnational legislation, despite ongoing variability in compliance. Consequently, the proportion of the global population covered by comprehensive smoke-free legislation has increased from 3% in 2007 to 33% in 2024, now covering 2·6 billion people. 8 The Americas stand out for both the scale of policy implementation and the magnitude of estimated reductions in exposure. details.title: Global and regional progress towards reduced burden of oral conditions between 2019 and 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Background WHO's Global Oral Health Action Plan (GOHAP) targets include a 10% relative reduction in the combined prevalence of main oral conditions by 2030. The first GOHAP evaluation was planned for 2023, with subsequent evaluations scheduled for 2026 and 2030. The aim of this systematic analysis of the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2023 was to evaluate global and regional progress (2019-23) towards this target and related complementary indicators. Methods Using modelled estimates from epidemiological surveys and registries in 204 countries and territories, we estimated the age-standardised prevalence of untreated caries in deciduous and permanent teeth, severe periodontitis, edentulism, other oral disorders and orofacial clefts, and the age-standardised incidence of lip and oral cavity cancer. Progress towards GOHAP targets was measured by comparing the percentage change from 2019 to 2023 in the above indicators against the stated GOHAP target of a 10% relative reduction. Findings Globally, the age-standardised prevalence of main oral conditions declined (-1·55% [95% uncertainty interval -2·32 to -0·82]) between 2019 and 2023, but global cases increased by 3·07% (2·32 to 3·75), from 3·62 billion (3·35 to 3·95) to 3·73 billion (3·45 to 4·06). Among complementary indicators, reductions in age-standardised prevalence were observed for untreated caries in permanent teeth (-1·99% [-2·49 to -1·40]) whereas the age-standardised incidence of lip and oral cavity cancer increased (8·35% [0·13 to 16·32]), as did the age-standardised prevalence of orofacial clefts (2·25% [0·77 to 3·83]). Progress was heterogeneous across GBD super-regions, with south Asia having the largest reductions in the age-standardised prevalence of main oral conditions (-3·34% [-4·95 to -1·80]) and untreated caries in deciduous teeth (-9·09% [-17·62 to -0·08]). Sub-Saharan Africa showed the largest increase in prevalent cases of main oral conditions (9·51% [8·09-10·94]) and age-standardised incidence of lip and oral cavity cancer (14·86% [1·19-32·45]). The high-income super-region had an increase in the age-standardised prevalence of main oral conditions (1·24% [0·56-1·96]) and untreated caries in deciduous teeth (9·21% [6·60-11·89]). Interpretation Our modelled estimates of global trends in the prevalence of oral conditions from 2019 to 2023 suggest that early progress is modest and, at the current pace, insufficient to meet the 2030 GOHAP targets. Accelerated, equity-focused prevention and integration of essential oral health-care services within primary care and universal health coverage are needed, alongside strengthened oral cancer control and congenital anomaly care. Funding The Gates Foundation.

details.title: Global and regional progress towards reduced burden of oral conditions between 2019 and 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Introduction Oral diseases are a foundational yet persistently underprioritised component of global health, with far-reaching implications for quality of life, health equity, and health systems worldwide. 1 , 2 , 3 Despite being largely preventable, the burden of oral diseases has remained high over the past three decades, 4 and its economic and social costs underscore the urgent need for robust, equitable global strategies. 5 Recognition of oral diseases within global public health agendas, including WHO's Global Oral Health Action Plan (GOHAP) and related policy initiatives, 6 , 7 reflects an imperative to embed oral disease prevention and health care in broader health systems to achieve sustainable improvements in population health. 8 , 9 , 10 The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) provides one of the few globally comparable resources for estimating the oral disease burden across locations and over time. 11 , 12 Data from GBD 2019 were instrumental in setting evidence-based targets within the WHO GOHAP 2023–2030. GOHAP is a call to action that outlines 11 global targets, six strategic objectives, and 100 recommended actions to be achieved by 2030. 6 The GOHAP monitoring framework establishes two key overarching global targets: to achieve universal coverage for oral health-care services (target A) and to reduce the oral disease burden (target B). Specifically, target B calls for a relative reduction of 10% by 2030 in the combined global prevalence of the main oral conditions over the life course. Ten complementary indicators accompany overarching global target B, six of which relate to reductions in the prevalence of untreated caries of deciduous teeth (indicator B.4), untreated caries of permanent teeth (B.5), severe periodontitis (B.6), edentulism (B.7), and orofacial clefts (B.9), and reductions in the incidence of lip and oral cavity cancer (B.8). WHO used data from GBD 2019 to establish baseline measures for the GOHAP targets. details.title: Global and regional progress towards reduced burden of oral conditions between 2019 and 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Methods Study overview This study was designed as a monitoring and accountability analysis of progress towards the GOHAP targets, rather than as a causal assessment of epidemiological change or policy effectiveness. Accordingly, the GBD estimates should be interpreted as modelled approximations that integrate diverse data sources and rely on explicit statistical assumptions. Additionally, the short observation window (2019–23), chosen to align with the GOHAP initial monitoring period, might limit the ability to detect structural changes in disease patterns and should be understood as reflecting early progress rather than long-term trends. This study was developed as part of the GBD Collaborator Network and GBD Protocol, 13 with support from the GBD Secretariat, the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME), and the GBD Oral Disorders Collaborator Network under IHME ID 6181. Ethical approval was not required for this study. The complete GBD methodology is available in the primary reports of GBD 2023 and their accompanying appendices. 14 , 15 Our study complies with the GATHER statement, 8 and the GATHER checklist is available in the appendix (p 38) . Data sources Seven oral conditions were evaluated: untreated caries in deciduous teeth; untreated caries in permanent teeth; severe periodontitis; edentulism; other oral disorders; lip and oral cavity cancer; and orofacial clefts. Case definitions and corresponding ICD-10 codes are shown in table 1 . The term main oral conditions refers to the combined group of untreated caries, severe periodontitis, edentulism, and other oral disorders. details.title: Global and regional progress towards reduced burden of oral conditions between 2019 and 2023: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023.
details.text: Discussion Coinciding with the first planned assessment of GOHAP targets, this analysis shows a modest improvement in the combined prevalence of main oral conditions that masks a still-expanding global burden. Against the GOHAP target of a 10% reduction by 2030, the combined age-standardised prevalence of main oral conditions fell by –1·55% between 2019 and 2023, yet cases rose by 3·07% to 3·73 billion, signalling that population growth and ageing are outpacing current prevention efforts and oral health-care service capacity. 18 Although most complementary targets are off track, it is important to recognise that they are not equally responsive to short-term policy change or health-system reorganisation. Thus, expectations for measurable progress should differ accordingly. Only untreated caries in permanent teeth showed a measurable decline (−1·99%), while lip and oral cavity cancers (8·35%) and orofacial clefts (2·25%) showed noticeable increases. This pattern is particularly salient given that, although they are less prevalent than the main oral conditions, lip and oral cavity cancer and orofacial clefts are the only oral conditions in GBD directly associated with mortality. Although these changes might reflect true epidemiological shifts, they could also be the result of improved surveillance, registry coverage, or reporting. This is particularly important for cancers and congenital anomalies, for which ascertainment sensitivity varies across regions. Progress towards the GOHAP targets was found to be highly uneven across regions, underscoring the need for region-specific policy responses rather than one-size-fits-all approaches. South Asia had the largest decline in the overarching target (−3·34%), a pace that need to be sustained to meet the 2030 targets, alongside reductions in several complementary indicators (ie, untreated caries in deciduous and permanent teeth, severe periodontitis, and edentulism). However, the incidence of lip and oral cavity cancer in south Asia increased markedly (14·33%). details.title: Support for Human and Civil Rights in Physical Disability, Mental Illness, and Substance Use Disorder.
details.text: Importance While there is much research on stigma toward marginalized populations, public perceptions regarding deservingness of basic human and civil rights of these groups have not been examined in a nationwide sample of US adults. Objective To understand the US public's perceptions regarding deservingness of basic human and contested civil rights for people with severe physical disabilities (SPDs), severe mental illness (SMI), and substance use disorders (SUDs). Design, setting, and participants This cross-sectional study was a nationwide US internet-based quota panel survey of US adults (aged ≥18 years) who completed the survey. Responses were collected from January 17 to February 12, 2025. Main outcomes and measures Participants rated their support for 5 human rights (adequate standard of living, high standards of health, legal capacity, freedom from torture, living independently) and 3 civil rights (being a parent, running for political office, owning a gun) for people with SPDs, SMI, and SUDs using a 5-point Likert scale, with marginalized subgroups presented to participants in randomized order. McNemar test for paired binary data was used to examine differences in mean support across subgroups, and linear probability regression models were used to identify demographic variables associated with support. Results In this survey of 1442 US adult participants (849 female [58.9%]; 588 male [40.8%]; 3 nonbinary [0.2%]; and 2 preferred not to say [0.1%]), the SPD subgroup received significantly higher support across all 5 human rights and 3 civil rights compared with SMI and SUD subgroups. For example, 79.0% (95% CI, 76.9%-81.2%) of participants supported the right to live independently for people with SPDs, while 67.0% supported this right for those with SMI (95% CI, 64.6%-69.5%) and 68.4% supported this right for those with SUDs (95% CI, 66.0%-70.9%). Civil rights received lower support across all 3 subgroups; for example, 40.1% (95% CI, 37.5%-42.6%) supported the right to run for political office for those with SMI and 41.4% (95% CI, 38.8%-44.0%) for those with SUDs compared with 62.7% (95% CI, 60.1%-65.2%) for those with SPDs. Democratic affiliation and lived experience with behavioral health care were associated with higher support for human rights (eg, among those with SUDs, up to 17.1 and 14.2 percentage points higher support, respectively). Male sex and younger age (18-24 years) were associated with greater support for civil rights (eg, male sex with 17.9 percentage points higher support for gun ownership among those with SPDs and age 18-24 years with a 27.1 percentage-point difference among those with SMI). Conclusions and relevance These findings contribute important evidence to the existing literature on stigma, highlighting discrepancies in public support for basic human and contested civil rights across marginalized subgroups, which can inform interventions to address public attitudes toward people with behavioral health conditions.

details.title: Patient Navigation and Postpartum Health Care Outcomes: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
details.text: Importance Postpartum care in the US is fragmented and inadequate, with major disparities in quality. Patient navigation is a promising health services intervention to improve health care provision and reduce disparities. Objective To evaluate whether postpartum patient navigation improved postpartum health care quality among people with low incomes. Design, setting, and participants This randomized clinical trial was conducted at a single urban academic medical center from January 2020 to July 2024 and included English- or Spanish-speaking pregnant people 16 years or older with Medicaid insurance. Data analysis started in October 2024. Intervention Participants were randomly assigned to 1 year of patient navigation vs usual care. Those randomized to navigation received individualized services that were designed to overcome postpartum-specific barriers to care from a trained lay navigator. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome, as ascertained from medical records, was receipt of 6 care elements considered to be essential to optimal postpartum care by 12 weeks postpartum. Secondary outcomes included the proportion of components received by 12 weeks and receipt of health services at 11 to 13 months. Results A total of 405 people (mean [SD] age, 28.2 [5.7] years; 10 [2%] were Asian, multiracial, or another race; 166 [41%] were Hispanic; 202 [50%] were non-Hispanic Black; and 27 [7%] were non-Hispanic White) were randomized (203 [50%] in patient navigation; 202 [50%] received usual care). The frequency of the primary outcome (ie, receipt of all 6 essential components of postpartum care) was similar between the groups (19 [9.4%] in patient navigation vs 16 [7.9%] in usual care; P = .60). However, the mean (SD) proportion of components received was significantly higher among navigation recipients (71% [17%] vs 64% [23%]; P = .002). Three components drove this difference: postpartum visit completion (195 [96%] vs 161 [80%]; P Conclusions The results of this randomized clinical trial suggest that although patient navigation did not result in a higher frequency of achieving all 6 components of postpartum care, the proportion of care components received was significantly higher. At 1 year postpartum, those randomized to patient navigation demonstrated multiple improved health services outcomes, including more frequent transition to primary care. details.title: Financial Effects of an Out-of-Pocket Cap in Traditional Medicare.
details.text: Importance Traditional Medicare (TM) exposes beneficiaries to substantial financial risk because, unlike Medicare Advantage (MA), there is no out-of-pocket (OOP) maximum for medical spending. Policymakers have proposed introducing an OOP cap, but its fiscal and behavioral effects are uncertain. Objective To estimate the financial impacts of introducing OOP spending caps of $3000, $5000, or $10 000 annually in TM on beneficiary costs, enrollment patterns, and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services expenditures between 2026 and 2034. Design, setting, and participants This economic evaluation using principles of microsimulation analysis projected enrollment, spending, and health care use outcomes under baseline (no OOP cap) and 3 alternative cap scenarios using publicly available national Medicare and insurance data from 2020 to 2024 with projections through 2034. The model incorporated elasticity-based behavioral responses, including beneficiary switching between TM and MA, changes in service use, and increases to MA benchmarks and spending. Sensitivity analyses varied model assumptions probabilistically. Exposure Introduction of annual OOP caps for Parts A and B in TM at $3000, $5000, or $10 000. Main outcomes and measures Projected changes in beneficiary enrollment by coverage type, mean annual beneficiary OOP and premium spending, and annual Medicare expenditures. Results Between 2026 and 2034, a $3000 OOP cap was projected to reduce mean annual beneficiary expenditures by $1568, compared with $1138 under a $5000 cap and $707 under a $10 000 cap. Corresponding increases in annual Medicare spending were estimated at $96 billion (90% simulation uncertainty interval [SUI], $80-$114 billion), $70 billion (90% SUI, $55-$85 billion), and $39 billion (90% SUI, $29-$50 billion), respectively. OOP caps, especially at lower thresholds, would substantially shift beneficiaries from MA to TM. Conclusions and relevance Results of this study suggest that implementing an OOP spending cap in TM would provide meaningful financial protection for beneficiaries but impose substantial fiscal costs on Medicare.

details.title: Combined impact of smoking, alcohol and social inequalities on premature mortality in urban India.
details.text: Associations with mortality of social inequalities, smoking and drinking differ widely between populations. Here we recruited 500,810 adults aged ≥35 years from Chennai city during 1998-2001 in South India and followed to 2020 for verbal-autopsy-assessed cause-specific mortality. Among those initially without chronic disease, multivariable-adjusted Cox regression (censored at age 70 years) related initial characteristics to mortality rates. Even among non-smoking non-drinkers, those with no schooling had almost three times the mortality rate ratio (RR) of those with >11 years education (men, RR of 2.76, 95% confidence interval (CI) 2.58-2.95; women, RR of 2.93, 95% CI 2.69-3.19), with substantial mortality excesses from each major disease category. These social inequalities were further exacerbated by much higher smoking and drinking prevalences among less educated men. Adjusted for education, male smoking (versus not, RR of 1.26, 95% CI 1.22-1.29) and drinking (versus not, RR of 1.52, 95% CI 1.48-1.56) were independently associated with risk and together almost doubled male mortality (both versus neither, RR of 1.89, 95% CI 1.84-1.94). Few women (<0.1%) smoked or drank.

details.title: Role of community and sexual contacts as drivers of MPXV clade I.
details.text: Initial investigation into the emerging mpox outbreak caused by novel monkeypox virus (MPXV) clade Ib in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has identified signs of sustained human-to-human transmission and epidemiological links to sexual contacts involving female sex workers (FSWs), which have not been observed in previous clade Ia outbreaks. Using mathematical models incorporating age-dependent contact patterns, we quantified the role of frequent sexual interactions as opposed to community contacts in clade Ib's dynamics and found that this additional mode of transmission could explain its increased outbreak potential compared with clade Ia. As with the globally circulating clade IIb, which is transmitted predominantly among men who have sex with men, our findings reinforce the importance of protecting key population groups-specifically FSWs for clade Ib-in controlling ongoing mpox outbreaks.

details.title: Mapping pesticide mixtures to cancer risk at the country scale with spatial exposomics.
details.text: Despite decades of concern over the carcinogenic potential of agricultural pesticides, toxicological studies relying on single endpoints have yet to establish a definitive link between environmental pesticide exposure and cancer in real-world contexts. Here we use an integrative spatial Bayesian framework that merges high-resolution environmental pesticide risk modelling with comprehensive cancer registry data to map pesticide-linked cancer clusters in Peru with unprecedented precision. Our process-based model, encompassing 31 key pesticide active ingredients, together with an innovative stratification of cancer cases by developmental lineage, reveals a robust spatial association between environmental pesticide exposure risk and cancer incidence. In pesticide-associated cancer hotspots, exposomic profiling of liver tissue-a primary target of chemical carcinogens-uncovers a distinct transcriptomic signature of pesticide exposure, implicating a non-genotoxic mode of action that disrupts core regulatory circuitries sustaining cell identity. Collectively, these findings strongly support a mechanistic link between pesticide exposure and cancer, challenging assumptions of human non-carcinogenicity derived from reductionist experimental models. This study redefines the exposome as a lineage-conditioned, mechanistically tractable framework and shows how complex pesticide mixtures can contribute to carcinogenic trajectories, with profound and far-reaching implications for global health policy and socio-ecological equity.

details.title: Predicting schistosome transmission in rural Uganda using water contact data from wearable GPS devices.
details.text: Granular spatial data and models of human behaviour are currently lacking for schistosomiasis. We collected ten days of wearable GPS logger data from 452 individuals in rural Uganda to model water contact as a proxy indicator of usage at 69 georeferenced open-water sites and 32 public taps or boreholes. Among participants, 63.9 and 33.2% visited at least one water site and tap or borehole, respectively. Exponential spatial decay models accurately predicted site-specific open-water contact (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve = 0.87) and tap or borehole usage (0.92). There was no evidence of tap or borehole usage influencing open-water contact. Incorporating mobility terciles did not improve simple spatial decay models. Integrating spatial decay-based estimates of open-water-site usage into an individual-based transmission model produced realistic estimates of one-year Schistosoma mansoni reinfection and provided a ranking of water sites contributing to transmission. Our spatial decay models offer scalable tools for focal interventions for schistosomiasis.

允许：
- 全半角标点规范化（中文语境下统一为全角标点，数字、英文、网址、代码除外）
- 破折号 / 连字符统一（`--`、`—`、`–` 按中文规范处理）

- 句首重复与句式单一化调整
- 段落结构与过渡、术语一致性
- 「学术腔」压缩——以清晰、准确为导向

**不允许：**
- 针对任何 AI 检测器做优化（即不以“降低 AI 检测分数”为目标）
- 承诺或尝试让 AI 生成的内容“通过编辑/审稿审查”
- 把 AI 生成内容伪装为人类原创
- 去除、篡改来源信息或元数据（如 C2PA 标签）
- 在报告或稿件中隐瞒 AI 使用情况

## 工作流程

1. **诊断**：通读全文，按下方清单逐项检查并记录问题位置。
2. **规范化**：逐项修改，保持原意不变，不做事实层面的增删（需要增删事实时留待作者本人处理）。
3. **输出**：给出「修改后全文 + 修改说明 + 建议作者人工复核的事项」。

## 诊断清单

- [ ] 全半角标点混用（如 `,` 应为 `，`；中文里的半角括号、冒号、问号）
- [ ] 全角字母 / 数字混入（应转半角，如 `ＡＢＣ` → `ABC`、`２０２６` → `2026`）
- [ ] 破折号不规范（`--`、单个 `—`、`–` 混用）
- [ ] 冗余套话：进行了、通过……的方式、在……的情况下、值得注意的是、需要指出的是、综上所述、总而言之等
- [ ] 长句（超过约 60 字的单句，提示拆分）
- [ ] 句首重复（相邻句以相同词语开头）
- [ ] 术语前后不一致
- [ ] 段落过长或主题混杂

## 输出格式

```
【修改后全文】
……

【修改说明】
1. 第 X 段：……（原因：……）
2. ……

【请作者人工复核】
- 事实与数据（润色不改事实，需作者核对）
- 引用出处
- AI 使用披露是否已写入稿件
```

## 使用提示

本 Skill 是写作质量工具。它不保证、也不尝试让文本“看起来不像 AI 写的”。如果你的稿件使用了 AI 辅助，请在稿件中如实披露（可配合普贤的披露声明生成器使用）。

English: Du, S. (2026). *Academic writing copyediting skill* [Skill definition]. https://naturedu.github.io/socialmedicine/.

# Skill：主动健康与健康融入万策（Health in All Policies，总纲旗舰）

**版本** 1.0 · **作者** 杜思娴 (Du Sixian) · **许可** MIT · **更新** 2026-10-23

## 用途

这是「普贤——社医卫管科研助手」方法学套件的**总纲旗舰 Skill**，承载整套工具的理念与整合逻辑：

> **就是为了每一个人的健康。**

以「主动健康」为策略主轴，以「健康融入所有政策（Health in All Policies, HiAP）」为治理框架，把本网站的理论方法、数据源、选题与院校四个板块蒸馏成一个可用于**学科建设、课题设计、政策评估与教学**的工作流。既有普度众生式的普惠愿景（健康不止于治病，而是让政策、环境与日常都向健康倾斜），又把愿景落到可算、可评、可复现的方法与代码上。每个环节都给出「方法 + 代码」，Stata / R 双轨。

## 适用范围（明确边界）

允许：
- 以 HiAP 框架组织跨部门健康政策研究与健康影响评估（HIA）
- 以主动健康视角设计行为与体系层面的干预与评估方案
- 用定量方法（归因负担、公平性、成本效果）为「健康融入万策」提供证据
- 指导选题、基金申报与学科方向的凝练

**不允许：**
- 把健康价值凌驾于其他正当政策目标之上做单边裁断（HiAP 是权衡与协同，不是否决权）
- 以模型结果冒充已发生的健康结局；归因是模型估计，需显式说明
- 用愿景口号替代证据；本 Skill 要求每个主张都有方法学支撑

## 理念：从「普度众生」到「健康普惠」

- **普贤愿景的现代转译**：菩萨度人是个体修为；卫生治理的健康普惠是制度修为。普贤的品牌底色由此而来——像海浪一样温柔地渗透每个领域。
- **主动健康**：健康的第一责任人是个体，但个体选择被环境塑造。主动健康 = 个体主动（运动、营养、心理、睡眠、社交等健康行为）+ 体系主动（环境、政策、服务与支付方式让健康选择成为默认选项）。
- **健康融入万策（HiAP）**：WHO 赫尔辛基声明（2013）的核心主张——健康与福祉由卫生部门之外的因素决定，因此所有政策都应系统考虑健康后果。八项原则：考虑健康与健康公平、共同受益、多部门参与、利益相关者参与、政策一致性、问责与透明度、基于证据、能力建设。中国的政策表达是「将健康融入所有政策」与「健康中国 2030」战略。

## 工作流程总览（五大板块）

1. 理论框架（主动健康 + HiAP + 健康社会决定因素）→ 2. 健康影响评估 HIA 方法 → 3. 数据源（全球健康数据库）→ 4. 选题与基金 → 5. 院校与学科建设。每个板块「方法 + 代码」。

---

### 板块 1：理论框架（怎么写进论文与标书）

**方法**：

- **立论三件套**：① 健康社会决定因素（WHO CSDH：日常生活条件 + 权力、金钱与资源的分配）说明「为什么健康问题出在卫生部门之外」；② HiAP 说明「政策杠杆在哪里」（教育、住房、交通、环境、社保、医保、食品）；③ 主动健康说明「个体与体系如何共同发力」。
- **论文中的用法**：理论框架部分按「决定因素 → 政策杠杆 → 主动健康机制」三段展开；讨论部分回扣「该政策是否把健康带进了决策」。
- **标书中的用法**：立项依据写「健康融入万策」的政策窗口（如《“健康中国 2030”规划纲要》把健康融入所有政策列为基本原则），研究目标写清楚要评估哪一类政策的健康与公平后果。

**代码**（政策文本快速摸底：关键词与主题结构，辅助而非替代人工阅读）：

```r
library(quanteda)
docs <- readtext::readtext("policy_texts/*.txt")          # 政策文件目录
corp <- corpus(docs)
toks <- tokens(corp, remove_punct = TRUE)
dfmat <- dfm(toks)
kw <- c("健康", "预防", "公平", "环境", "医疗", "保障")
dfm_select(dfmat, pattern = kw) |> textstat_frequency()    # 政策文本中的健康话语频次
```

---

### 板块 2：健康影响评估（HIA）方法

**方法**：HIA 六步——① 筛选（是否值得做 HIA）；② 界定（范围、人群、时间、评估者）；③ 评估（基线、影响识别、定量/定性分析）；④ 建议（可执行的政策修改）；⑤ 报告；⑥ 监测与评价。

**定量核心公式**：

- 暴露—反应归因：人群归因分数 PAF = p(RR−1) / [p(RR−1) + 1]，p 为暴露率，RR 为暴露—反应相对危险度（来自系统综述/GBD 比较风险评估）。
- 归因负担 = 基线疾病负担 × PAF；干预后负担 = 基线负担 × (1 − 干预后暴露变化 × 归因系数)，据此算「可避免的死亡/DALY」。
- 公平性：集中指数 CI = 2·cov(y, r)/ȳ（r 为按社会经济排序的分数秩），并用分解说明政策收益分布。

**代码**：

```stata
* Stata：PAF 与可避免负担的情景计算
local p  0.35            // 基线暴露率
local RR 1.45            // 暴露-反应 RR（示例，来自 Meta 分析）
local paf = (`p'*(`RR'-1))/(`p'*(`RR'-1)+1)
di "PAF = " %5.3f `paf'
local B 12000            // 基线年死亡数（示例）
di "基线归因死亡 = " %9.0f (`B'*`paf')
* 干预使暴露率降至 0.25
local p2 0.25
local paf2 = (`p2'*(`RR'-1))/(`p2'*(`RR'-1)+1)
di "干预后可避免死亡 = " %9.0f (`B'*(`paf'-`paf2'))

* 公平性：集中指数（协方差法）
egen r = rank(y)         // y 为健康结局，按经济状况排序后的秩
sum y
gen lhs = 2*y*r/r(mean)
quietly reg lhs r
di "CI = " %5.3f _b[r]
```

```r
# R：同一计算 + 集中指数 + 情景比较
paf <- function(p, RR) p*(RR-1)/(p*(RR-1)+1)
B <- 12000
base  <- B * paf(0.35, 1.45)
after <- B * paf(0.25, 1.45)
avoid <- base - after
cat(sprintf("基线归因死亡 %.0f；干预后可避免死亡 %.0f\n", base, avoid))

# 集中指数
ci <- function(y, x) 2 * cov(y, rank(x)) / mean(y)
ci(health_y, income_x)
```

---

### 板块 3：数据源（健康融入万策的证据底座）

**方法**：按「问题 → 数据」配表。疾病负担用 GBD（IHME）；暴露与政策用 WHO GHO / 世界银行 HNP / 中国卫生健康统计年鉴；行为与主动健康用 CHARLS / CFPS / 中国居民营养与慢性病状况报告；环境暴露用中国 CDC 公卫数据中心与卫星产品；政策文本用各级政府公开文件。

**代码**（R 抓取与整理公开数据的习惯写法）：

```r
library(readxl)
df <- read_excel("GBD_results.xlsx")     # 从 GBD Results Tool 导出的 CSV/XLSX
agg <- aggregate(deaths ~ year + location, data = df, sum)
# 与政策时点对齐：政策前后负担变化（配合 ITS/DID skill 做因果评估）
```

> 完整数据库导航见网站「数据源」模块（25 个数据源，含链接与口径提示）。

---

### 板块 4：选题与基金（把愿景变成课题）

**方法**：主动健康 × HiAP 的选题生成规则——「政策杠杆 × 健康结局 × 公平维度」三维交叉。示例选题（直接可用）：

1. 医保支付方式改革（DRG/DIP）对预防服务供给与慢病并发症的影响（DID/ITS）
2. 「体医融合」运动处方纳入医保对慢病患者健康行为的因果效应（RCT/准实验）
3. 城市更新与 15 分钟生活圈对居民体力活动与肥胖的准实验评估（DID）
4. 学校供餐营养政策对儿童超重与学业表现的长期影响（队列/自然实验）
5. 气候政策（碳氮协同治理）的健康协同收益测算（CEA + PAF 归因）
6. 主动健康干预（五处方：运动/营养/心理/睡眠/社交）的社区整群随机试验
7. 健康影响评估制度化的国际比较与本土路径（政策文本分析 + 比较案例）
8. 远程医疗与数字健康工具对基层慢病管理的公平性影响（集中指数 + 分解）
9. 健康城市指标体系构建与考核的德尔菲研究
10. 食品标签/含糖饮料政策对健康不平等的异质性影响（fsQCA/分层分析）

**基金申报**：国自然（管理科学部 G04 健康管理与政策；医学部 H30）、国社科（社会学/应用经济/管理学）、教育部人文社科、卫健委委托课题——申报导航见网站「选题基金」模块；方法学技术路线直接引用本套件对应 Skill（DCE/Markov/DID/ITS/Meta 等）。

---

### 板块 5：院校与学科建设

**方法**：学科建设三件事——方向凝练（用本 Skill 五板块做教研室/课题组的方向地图）、人才培养（把 socialmedicineskills 速查手册作为研究生方法学课程大纲）、院际合作（按「院校科普」模块的 12 所院系匹配合作对象与报考方向）。代表学者路径的启示：把本地证据连接到全球数据与政策问题（借鉴 Science 卫生政策样本中作者路径一节）。

> 院校科普（北大公卫、复旦公卫、人大公管、人大人口与健康、浙大公卫、华科医管、武大政管、安医大等 12 所）见网站「院校」模块。

---

## 常见错误清单

- [ ] 把 HiAP 写成「卫生部门否决其他部门」，忽略共同受益与权衡
- [ ] PAF 计算用错暴露率口径（点暴露率 vs 累积暴露）或 RR 来源不明
- [ ] 把模型归因结果写成已发生的健康结局
- [ ] 只算平均效果，不报公平性分布（集中指数/分人群）
- [ ] 数据源口径混用（GBD 归因 vs 本地监测）
- [ ] 政策文本分析用词频代替人工阅读与制度分析
- [ ] 选题只有愿景没有可检验的因果问题
- [ ] 引用 GBD/WHO 数据未注明版本与年份

## 输出格式（政策健康影响评估报告模板）

```
【政策与背景】
政策名称、出台部门、目标与「健康融入万策」的关联点。

【HIA 界定】
范围、人群（含易受影响人群）、时间范围、评估者与利益相关者。

【基线】
暴露率、疾病负担、公平性现状（附数据源与版本）。

【影响评估】
暴露-反应证据（RR 与来源）；PAF 与可避免负担的情景计算；公平性影响（CI 与分解）；不确定性说明。

【建议】
可执行的政策修改建议（按证据强度分级）。

【监测与评价】
指标、数据来源与复查时点。
```

## 使用提示

- 本 Skill 是总纲：理论用「板块 1」、定量用「板块 2」、数据用「板块 3」、选题用「板块 4」、学科建设用「板块 5」；深度方法到对应 Skill（DCE 设计助手、Markov 模型助手、DID/ITS/DDD、Meta 分析、机器学习、卫生经济学教程）。
- 主动健康干预评估优先考虑整群随机试验与准实验设计；因果估计与模型归因分开表述。
- 愿景要有边界：健康融入万策是权衡的艺术，不是健康的一票否决。

---

# Skill：DCE 设计助手（离散选择实验设计与分析，Stata / R）

**版本** 1.0 · **作者** 杜思娴 (Du Sixian) · **许可** MIT · **更新** 2026-10-23

## 用途

一份可复用的「离散选择实验（Discrete Choice Experiment, DCE）」设计—分析工作流：从属性与水平设定、正交 / D-效率实验设计、选择集构造与分块，到 Stata（`clogit` / `mixlogit` / `lclogit2`）与 R（`mlogit` / `gmnl`）的模型估计、支付意愿（WTP）计算与结果报告。**每一步都给出「方法 + 代码」**，可直接作为提示词喂给大语言模型，也可作为操作手册照做。

## 适用范围（明确边界）

允许：
- 帮助研究者完成 DCE 全流程的设计与分析（健康经济学、环境经济学、交通、市场营销等陈述性偏好研究）
- 给出正交主效应设计、部分因子设计、D-效率设计的方法与 Stata/R 代码
- 用条件 logit（clogit）、混合 logit（mixlogit）、潜类别模型（latent class）估计偏好与 WTP

**不允许：**
- 替研究者做属性与水平的最终专业判断（需领域专家意见与利益相关者访谈支撑）
- 承诺设计或结果一定可发表；不替代计量经济学教科书与期刊审稿要求
- 在未检验 IIA、未说明分布假设的情况下武断下结论

## 软件准备

方法：Stata 17 及以上、R ≥ 4.2。分析命令 `mixlogit`、`lclogit2`、`dcreate` 来自 SSC（作者 Arne Hole）；R 侧用 `DoE.base`（正交表）、`AlgDesign`（D-效率设计）、`mlogit` / `gmnl`（分析）。

```stata
* Stata（联网安装一次）
ssc install mixlogit, replace
ssc install lclogit2, replace
ssc install dcreate,  replace
```

```r
# R
install.packages(c("DoE.base", "AlgDesign", "support.CEs", "mlogit", "gmnl"))
```

## 工作流程总览（8 步）

1. 确定属性与水平 → 2. 正交 / D-效率实验设计 → 3. 设计质量检查 → 4. 选择集构造与分块 → 5. 问卷与预测试 → 6. 样本量与 long 数据整理 → 7. clogit / mixlogit / 潜类别估计 → 8. 解读与报告。以下每一步均为「方法 + 代码」。

---

### 第 1 步：确定属性与水平

**方法**：文献综述 + 定性访谈（专家、患者/消费者、决策者）确定候选属性；一般 4–7 个属性、每个 2–4 个水平。水平需可实现、可理解、覆盖现实政策范围；「价格 / 费用」属性建议连续或至少 3 个水平，便于计算 WTP。全因子规模 = 各属性水平数相乘，用于判断是否需要缩减设计。

**代码**：

```stata
* Stata：生成 2^4 全因子（16 行），用于观察所有组合
clear
set obs 16
gen a = mod(_n-1, 2)              // 0/1
gen b = mod(int((_n-1)/2), 2)
gen c = mod(int((_n-1)/4), 2)
gen d = mod(int((_n-1)/8), 2)
list
```

```r
# R：属性水平表与全因子规模
levels <- list(费用 = c(10, 30, 50),   # 元/次
               候诊 = c(1, 3, 7),      # 天
               连续性 = c(0, 1),       # 0=不同医生 1=同一医生
               目录 = c(0, 1))         # 0=基础目录 1=扩展目录
sapply(levels, length)                 # 各属性水平数
full <- expand.grid(levels)            # 全因子组合
nrow(full)                             # 3*3*2*2 = 36
```

---

### 第 2 步：正交设计与 D-效率设计

**方法**：

- **正交主效应设计（orthogonal main-effects plan）**：在「主效应可估」前提下，把全因子压缩进正交表 Ln(m^k)（如 L8(2^7)、L9(3^4)、L36(2^11×3^12)）。要求：每列各水平出现次数相等（水平平衡），任意两列的水平组合出现次数相等（相关 = 0）。
- **部分因子设计 2^(k-p)**：用生成元压缩。例：4 个两水平属性取 8 行、生成元 d = a×b×c（模 2），得到分辨率 IV 设计——主效应相互正交，且不与任何两因子交互混杂。
- **D-效率设计（推荐，可充分利用先验、能排除不可行组合）**：极大化信息矩阵行列式。Stata 用 `dcreate`，R 用 `AlgDesign::optFederov` / `idefix`，商业软件可用 Ngene 或 SAS PROC OPTEX。

**代码**：

```stata
* Stata：2^(4-1) 分辨率 IV 正交主效应设计（8 行，生成元 d = a*b*c 模 2）
clear
set obs 16
gen a = mod(_n-1, 2)
gen b = mod(int((_n-1)/2), 2)
gen c = mod(int((_n-1)/4), 2)
gen d = mod(int((_n-1)/8), 2)
keep if mod(a+b+c+d, 2) == 0
list, sep(0)

* Stata：3^4 的 L9 正交设计（9 行）
clear
set obs 27
gen a = mod(_n-1, 3)
gen b = mod(int((_n-1)/3), 3)
gen c = mod(int((_n-1)/9), 3)
keep if mod(a+b+c, 3) == 0

* Stata：D-效率设计（dcreate，SSC）。示例：3 个属性、每选择集 2 个方案、12 个选择集
matrix b0 = J(1, 3, 0)                    // 先验参数（默认 0）
dcreate i.x1 i.x2 i.x3, nalt(2) nset(12) bmat(b0) seed(2026)
* 注：dcreate 要求因子变量写法；详细选项以 help dcreate 为准
```

```r
# R：正交主效应设计（DoE.base）
library(DoE.base)
des24 <- oa.design(nlevels = c(2, 2, 2, 2))    # 2^4 → 8 行 L8
des33 <- oa.design(nlevels = c(3, 3, 3, 3))    # 3^4 → 9 行 L9
as.data.frame(des24)

# R：D-效率设计（AlgDesign）
library(AlgDesign)
full36 <- expand.grid(x1 = c(0, 1, 2), x2 = c(0, 1, 2), x3 = c(0, 1), x4 = c(0, 1))
dopt <- optFederov(~ ., data = full36, nTrials = 16, criterion = "D")
dopt$design                                  # 选中的 16 个 profile
dopt$D                                       # D-效率值
```

---

### 第 3 步：检查设计质量

**方法**：四项检查——① 正交性：任意两列相关 ≈ 0；② 水平平衡：每列各水平出现次数相等；③ 无主导（dominance）：同一选择集内不存在「在所有属性上都不差于另一方案」的方案；④ 效率：D-效率尽可能高（可与全因子对照）。不通过则换正交表、换生成元或增加行数。

**代码**：

```stata
* Stata：水平平衡 + 两两相关
tab1 a b c d
pwcorr a b c d
```

```r
# R：水平平衡、相关矩阵与设计效率
apply(des24, 2, table)                       # 水平平衡
round(cor(as.data.frame(des24)), 3)          # 正交性：非对角应 ≈ 0
eval.design(~ ., dopt$design)                # AlgDesign：方差膨胀、D/G 效率
```

---

### 第 4 步：构造选择集与分块

**方法**：把设计行**两两随机配对**组成选择集（典型：2 个方案 + 1 个 opt-out「都不选」）；配对时避免重复组合与主导对。每名受访者作答 6–10 个选择集；超过问卷容量则**分块（block）**，块间随机分配给受访者。选择集顺序、方案左右位置均随机化，并生成多个问卷版本。

**代码**：

```r
# R：随机配对、分块
library(dplyr)
set.seed(2026)
prof  <- as.data.frame(des24) |> sample_frac(1)      # 随机打乱
pairs <- matrix(seq_len(nrow(prof)), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)
nset  <- nrow(pairs)                                  # 选择集数
nblock <- 2; per <- 2                                 # 2 个块、每块 2 题
block  <- rep(1:nblock, each = per, length.out = nset)
out <- data.frame(choice_set = rep(1:nset, each = 2),
                  block = rep(block, each = 2),
                  alt = rep(1:2, times = nset),
                  prof[as.vector(t(pairs)), ])
# opt-out 在问卷中额外提供“都不选”；数据里记 alt == 3、各属性 = 0
```

```stata
* Stata：为每个选择集追加 opt-out 行（alt == 3，属性全为 0）
local nset 4
forvalues s = 1/`nset' {
    set obs `=_N+1'
    replace choice_set = `s' if _n == _N
    replace alt = 3 if _n == _N
    foreach v in a b c d {
        replace `v' = 0 if _n == _N
    }
}
```

---

### 第 5 步：问卷与预测试

**方法**：预测试分两轮——① think-aloud 认知访谈 5–10 人，检查属性表述是否被正确理解；② 小样本 30–50 份，检查：是否存在「永远选同一方案 / 永远选 opt-out」的受访者、是否有主导选项、任务负担与完成时间是否合理。据结果修正水平、措辞或题数。

**代码**：

```stata
* Stata：预测试数据体检——受访者选择 opt-out 的次数分布
egen n_optout = total(choice == 1 & alt == 3), by(id)
tab n_optout
* 提示：某受访者所有题都选 opt-out，说明属性或任务设计可能有问题
```

```r
# R：同一检查
library(dplyr)
dat |> group_by(id) |>
  summarise(n_optout = sum(choice == 1 & alt == 3),
            n_A      = sum(choice == 1 & alt == 1),
            n_total  = n_distinct(choice_set))
```

---

### 第 6 步：样本量与 long 数据整理

**方法**：

- **样本量**（Orme 经验法则）：n ≥ 500 × c / (t × a)，其中 c = 水平数最多的属性的水平数，t = 每受访者选择集数，a = 每选择集方案数（不含 opt-out）。例：c = 3、t = 8、a = 2 → n ≥ 500×3/16 ≈ 94；正式研究按预算与检验力要求上调。
- **数据格式**：long（长表），每行 = 受访者 × 选择集 × 方案；必需变量 `id`、`choice_set`、`alt`、`choice`（1/0）与各属性取值；opt-out 行属性全为 0。
- **编码**：连续属性用原始数值；分类属性用 effects coding（-1/0/1）或虚拟变量，全流程保持一致，报告时注明。

**代码**：

```stata
* Stata：示例 long 数据（1 名受访者、2 个选择集、各 3 个方案）
clear
input id choice_set alt choice a b c d
1 1 1 1 0 0 1 1
1 1 2 0 1 1 0 0
1 1 3 0 0 0 0 0
1 2 1 0 1 0 1 0
1 2 2 1 0 1 0 1
1 2 3 0 0 0 0 0
end

* 宽表 → 长表（宽表每行一个选择集，选项变量带后缀 _1/_2/_3）
reshape long choice_ a_ b_ c_ d_, i(id choice_set) j(alt)
rename (choice_ a_ b_ c_ d_) (choice a b c d)

* effects coding 示例：三水平属性 a（0/1/2 → -1/0/1）
recode a (0 = -1) (1 = 0) (2 = 1)
```

```r
# R：dfidx 构造选择数据（mlogit 用）
library(mlogit)
md <- dfidx(dat, idx = c("id", "alt"), choice = "choice")
```

---

### 第 7 步：模型估计（Stata 与 R 对应）

#### 7.1 条件 logit（`clogit`）

**方法**：随机效用模型 U = β'x + ε，ε 为独立同分布 I 型极值分布，则方案选择概率 P = exp(V)/Σexp(V)。适用前提是 IIA（无关方案独立性）；可用「子集删除」的系数稳定性直觉检验。违反 IIA → 改用 mixlogit 或潜类别模型。同一受访者的多个选择相关，标准误需 `vce(cluster id)`。**WTP = −β_属性 / β_费用**（费用系数为负）。

**代码**：

```stata
clogit choice a b c d, group(choice_set) vce(cluster id)
est store clogit

* WTP：d 为费用属性时的属性 b 的 WTP（delta 方法，含 95% CI）
nlcom wtp_b: -_b[b] / _b[d]

* IIA 直觉检验：删除 opt-out 后系数应大体稳定
clogit choice a b c d if alt != 3, group(choice_set) vce(cluster id)
```

```r
# R：clogit（survival）与 mlogit 等价实现
library(survival)
clogit(choice ~ a + b + c + d + strata(choice_set), data = dat)

library(mlogit)
m1 <- mlogit(choice ~ a + b + c + d | 0, data = md)
summary(m1)
```

#### 7.2 混合 logit（`mixlogit`）

**方法**：允许系数在个体间服从分布（正态 / 对数正态等），捕捉**偏好异质性**；随机系数 SD 显著即存在异质性。费用属性常用对数正态（保持负号），抽样用 Halton 序列 `nrep(500)`。与 clogit 比较 AIC/BIC（`fitstat`）判断是否需要异质性设定。

**代码**：

```stata
* 随机系数：a、b、c 正态，d 固定
mixlogit choice a b c d, group(choice_set) id(id) rand(a b c) nrep(500)
est store mixl
fitstat                                     // AIC/BIC，与 clogit 比较

* 对数正态费用 + 相关随机参数（ln(1) = rand() 中第 1 个随机参数取对数正态）
mixlogit choice a b c d, group(choice_set) id(id) rand(a b c) ln(1) corr nrep(500)

* WTP：mixlwtp（SSC）或 delta 方法；具体语法以 help mixlwtp 为准
```

```r
# R：混合 logit（mlogit rpar）
m2 <- mlogit(choice ~ a + b + c + d | 0, data = md,
             rpar = c(a = "n", b = "n", c = "n"),
             R = 500, halton = NA, panel = TRUE)
summary(m2)
```

#### 7.3 潜类别 logit（latent class，`lclogit2`）

**方法**：假设存在 K 个不可观测的偏好类别，各类别内系数不同（类别内同质、类别间异质）。**类别数 K 用 BIC/AIC 选择**（`lclogit2` 默认输出）。类成员平均概率用 `lclogitprob`；刻画「谁属于哪类」可用类成员协变量模型 `lclogitml`（成员方程放入年龄、收入等），或事后与个体特征交叉描述。

**代码**：

```stata
lclogit2 choice a b c d, group(choice_set) id(id) nclasses(2) seed(2026)
lclogit2, nclasses(3) seed(2026)            // 比较 BIC/AIC 选类别数
est store lc3
lclogitprob, cpprob(3)                      // 各类别平均成员概率
estat lcmean, post                          // 各类别协变量均值（刻画类别特征）

* 类成员协变量模型（membership 方程放入 age、income）
lclogitml choice a b c d, group(choice_set) id(id) nclasses(3) membership(age income)

* WTP：lcwtp（lclogit2 附带），语法以 help lcwtp 为准；
* 或手工取各类别系数比值并配合 delta 方法
```

```r
# R：潜类别 logit（gmnl）
library(gmnl)
lc <- gmnl(choice ~ a + b + c + d | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1, data = md,
           model = "lc", panel = TRUE, Q = 3)
summary(lc)
```

---

### 第 8 步：结果解读与报告

**方法**：

- **主表**：clogit / mixlogit / 潜类别三模型并列，报系数（SE）；mixlogit 报均值与 SD；潜类别报各类别系数与成员概率。
- **WTP 表**：WTP = −β_x / β_cost，95% CI 用 delta 方法（`nlcom`）或 Krinsky-Robb（`mixlwtp` 等），报告所用方法。
- **文字结论**：系数方向与显著性 → 政策含义；SD 显著或类别差异 → 细分人群偏好。
- **报告规范**：建议对照 ISPOR conjoint checklist：属性与水平依据、设计类型与效率、预测试、估计方法与分布假设、WTP 区间。

**代码**：

```stata
* WTP 与置信区间（clogit，delta 方法）
nlcom wtp_b: -_b[b] / _b[d], post
estimates store wtp_b

* 三模型并列输出
estimates table clogit mixl lc3, b(%9.3f) se stats(N aic bic)
```

```r
# R：delta 方法 WTP（car::deltaMethod）
library(car)
deltaMethod(coef(m1), "-b/d")               # 按实际系数名替换 b、d
```

---

## 常见错误清单

- [ ] 用 `mlogit` 当 `clogit` 用（未指定 `group()` / `strata()`）→ 系数有偏
- [ ] 忘记 `vce(cluster id)` → 标准误低估
- [ ] opt-out 编码不一致（有的 0、有的缺失）
- [ ] effects coding 与虚拟变量混用、编码前后不一致
- [ ] 不检验 IIA 就下结论
- [ ] 把分类水平的 1/2/3 直接当连续变量解释
- [ ] 未报告设计类型、效率与预测试信息
- [ ] mixlogit 随机分布选择无依据（如费用却用对称正态）

## 输出格式（分析报告模板）

```
【设计与数据】
属性/水平表；设计类型（正交 / D-效率）与效率值；选择集与块数；预测试结果；样本量与法则依据。

【模型估计】
表 1：clogit 主结果；表 2：mixlogit 均值 + SD；表 3：潜类别各类别系数与成员概率（附 AIC/BIC 选 K 的依据）。

【WTP】
WTP = -β_x / β_cost 及 95% CI（注明 delta / Krinsky-Robb 方法）。

【结论与局限】
方向性结论 + 偏好异质性 + 局限（IIA、分布假设、设计假设、外部效度）。
```

## 使用提示

- 命令与选项随版本更新，运行 `help clogit` / `help mixlogit` / `help lclogit2` / `help dcreate` 核对。
- 设计阶段建议流程：先全因子/正交表做基线，再用 `dcreate` 或 `AlgDesign` 做 D-效率设计，比较 D 值后定稿。
- 本 Skill 提供方法与代码模板；研究背景、属性取舍与最终结论由研究者负责。

# Skill：三重差分助手（DDD 政策效果评估，Stata / R）

**版本** 1.0 · **作者** 杜思娴 (Du Sixian) · **许可** MIT · **更新** 2026-10-23

## 用途

一份可复用的「三重差分（Difference-in-Difference-in-Differences, DDD）」政策效果评估工作流：当 DID 的平行趋势在某一维度不成立时，引入第三个维度做双重剔除，用三重交互项识别政策净效应。贯穿示例：「国家药品集中带量采购对公立医院（vs 民营医院）集采品种（vs 非集采品种）药品费用的影响」，三维 = 时间 × 医院类型 × 品种类型。**每一步都给出「方法 + 代码」**（Stata `reg` / `reghdfe` / `permute` 与 R `fixest::feols`），并内置一套**自洽的模拟面板数据**（60 家医院 × 2 类药品 × 2 期，真实 DDD 效应 δ = −8 万元/月）贯穿全流程，可直接作为提示词喂给大语言模型，也可作为操作手册照做。

## 适用范围（明确边界）

允许：
- 帮助卫生政策评估研究者完成 DDD 的设定、估计、分解验证、稳健性检验与报告（社会医学、卫生经济学、药物经济学等）
- 用 Stata / R 生成模拟面板数据、估计三重交互模型、做两个 2×2 DID 的分解表与安慰剂检验
- 给出 DDD 识别假设（偏误同质性）、第三维度选择标准与事件研究式动态检验思路

**不允许：**
- 替研究者做「第三维度是否外生」「政策时点如何界定」的最终专业判断（需政策文件与领域知识支撑）
- 承诺 DDD 一定优于 DID 或结果一定可发表；不替代计量经济学教科书（Wooldridge、Angrist & Pischke 等）与期刊审稿要求
- 在未交代识别假设、未做分解表与稳健性检验的情况下武断下结论

## 软件准备

方法：Stata 17 及以上、R ≥ 4.2。Stata 侧 `reghdfe`（高维固定效应，作者 Sergio Correia）来自 SSC，依赖包 `ftools` 会随之自动安装；R 侧用 `fixest`（作者 Laurent Bergé，`feols` 支持固定效应 + 聚类稳健标准误）。所有命令与选项随版本更新，不确定处以 `help` / 帮助文档为准。

```stata
* Stata（联网安装一次）
ssc install reghdfe, replace
* 若 ftools 未被自动装上：ssc install ftools, replace
```

```r
# R
install.packages("fixest")
```

## 工作流程总览（7 步）

0. 构造贯穿全程的模拟面板数据（60 医院 × 2 品种 × 2 期，内置真实 DDD 效应）→ 1. 从 DID 到 DDD：动机 → 2. 模型设定与估计 → 3. 核心系数 δ 的解读与分解验证 → 4. 平行趋势与稳健性 → 5. 多期扩展简述 → 6. 报告清单。以下每一步均为「方法 + 代码」。

---

### 第 0 步：构造模拟面板数据（贯穿全流程）

**方法**：60 家医院（id 1–30 公立、31–60 民营）× 2 类药品（集采品种 / 非集采品种）× 2 期（政策前 / 政策后），共 240 个观测；结局 y = 月均药品费用（万元）。数据生成过程（DGP）为真实线性模型，**内置真实 DDD 效应 δ = −8**，并内置两个「偏误源」：γ12 = −6（公立医院特有趋势，如 DRG 付费、取消药品加成等同期政策）、γ23 = −4（集采品种特有趋势，如专利到期、临床替代）。每家医院加医院层面随机效应 u_i ~ N(0, 4²)，制造院内相关（这正是聚类的依据），再加个体噪声 ε ~ N(0, 2²)。另外生成两个稳健性结局（第 4 步用）：y_qty = 集采品种采购数量（相关结局，真实效应 δ = −3）、y_dev = 与药品无关的耗材费用（安慰剂结局，真实效应 δ = 0）。

**代码**：

```stata
* ============ 第 0 步：模拟面板数据（贯穿全流程） ============
clear all
set seed 2026

* 60 家医院：id 1-30 公立（treated = 1），31-60 民营（treated = 0）
set obs 60
gen id = _n
gen treated = (id <= 30)          // 处理维度：1 = 公立医院（受集采约束）
gen u_i = rnormal(0, 4)           // 医院层面随机效应（制造院内相关，聚类依据）

* 每家医院 2 类药品：group = 1 集采品种，0 非集采品种
expand 2
bysort id: gen group = _n - 1

* 每个（医院 × 品种）2 期：post = 0 政策前，1 政策后
expand 2
bysort id group: gen post = _n - 1
gen time = post                   // 供 reghdfe absorb() 使用

* ---------- 真实数据生成过程（DGP，内置真实 DDD 效应 δ = -8） ----------
* y = γ0 + γ1·treated + γ2·post + γ3·group
*     + γ12·treated×post + γ13·treated×group + γ23·post×group
*     + δ·treated×post×group + u_i + ε
local g0 100                        // 基组均值（民营 × 非集采 × 政策前）
local g1 10                         // 公立医院整体费用水平更高
local g2 -5                         // 全体时间趋势（普遍控费）
local g3 20                         // 集采品种用量大、费用更高
local g12 -6                        // 偏误 1：公立医院特有趋势（DRG / 取消加成等）
local g13 5                         // 公立医院对集采品种的固定偏好
local g23 -4                        // 偏误 2：集采品种特有趋势（专利到期等）
local delta -8                      // 真实 DDD 效应：集采使公立医院集采品种额外下降 8 万元/月

gen y = `g0' + `g1'*treated + `g2'*post + `g3'*group + ///
        `g12'*treated*post + `g13'*treated*group + `g23'*post*group + ///
        `delta'*treated*post*group + u_i + rnormal(0, 2)

* ---------- 稳健性结局（第 4 步用） ----------
* y_qty：集采品种采购数量（相关结局，真实效应较小 δ = -3）
gen y_qty = 60 + 8*treated - 4*post + 18*group - 3*treated*post + ///
            4*treated*group - 2*post*group - 3*treated*post*group + ///
            u_i + rnormal(0, 3)
* y_dev：与药品无关的耗材费用（安慰剂结局，真实 δ = 0）
gen y_dev = 40 + 5*treated - 2*post + 2*group + 1*treated*post - ///
            1*treated*group + 0.5*post*group + 0*treated*post*group + ///
            0.5*u_i + rnormal(0, 5)

* 数据体检：8 组均值表（Stata 17+；16 及更早用 bysort treated post group: summarize y）
table treated post group, stat(mean y) stat(sd y) nototals
* 期望组均值（噪声平均掉后）：民营 非集采 前 100 / 后 95；民营 集采 前 120 / 后 111；
*                             公立 非集采 前 110 / 后 99；公立 集采 前 135 / 后 112
```

```r
# ============ 第 0 步：模拟面板数据（贯穿全流程） ============
set.seed(2026)
N <- 60                                     # 60 家医院
dat <- expand.grid(id = 1:N, group = c(0, 1), post = c(0, 1))
dat$treated <- as.integer(dat$id <= 30)     # 处理维度：1 = 公立医院
dat$u_i     <- rnorm(N, 0, 4)[dat$id]       # 医院层面随机效应（聚类依据）
dat$time    <- dat$post                     # 供 fixest 吸收固定效应

# 真实参数（内置真实 DDD 效应 delta = -8）
g0 <- 100; g1 <- 10; g2 <- -5; g3 <- 20
g12 <- -6; g13 <- 5; g23 <- -4; delta <- -8

dat$y <- with(dat, g0 + g1*treated + g2*post + g3*group +
                   g12*treated*post + g13*treated*group + g23*post*group +
                   delta*treated*post*group + u_i + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 2))

# 稳健性结局：y_qty（相关结局，真实 δ = -3）；y_dev（安慰剂结局，真实 δ = 0）
dat$y_qty <- with(dat, 60 + 8*treated - 4*post + 18*group - 3*treated*post +
                      4*treated*group - 2*post*group - 3*treated*post*group +
                      u_i + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 3))
dat$y_dev <- with(dat, 40 + 5*treated - 2*post + 2*group + 1*treated*post -
                      1*treated*group + 0.5*post*group + 0*treated*post*group +
                      0.5*u_i + rnorm(nrow(dat), 0, 5))

# 8 组均值表（应与下方期望值接近）
aggregate(y ~ treated + post + group, data = dat, FUN = mean)
```

---

### 第 1 步：从 DID 到 DDD：动机

**方法**：

- **两个潜在偏误需要双重剔除**。本例若做单维 DID，任一维度都面临威胁：① 用「公立 vs 民营」做 DID（只看集采品种）——公立医院同时经历 DRG 付费改革、取消药品加成等**只作用于公立医院、不区分品种**的政策，其费用趋势与民营医院本来就不同（DGP 里 γ12 = −6）；② 用「集采品种 vs 非集采品种」做 DID（只看公立医院）——集采品种因专利到期、临床替代等**与医院类型无关**的原因费用下行（DGP 里 γ23 = −4）。两个威胁方向一致、大小不明，单维 DID 都会把它们混进政策效应里。
- **三重交互 δ 的经济含义**：δ = 政策在「处理维度 × 第三维度」上的**增量**效果——公立医院集采品种费用在政策后的额外变化，同时剔除 (a) 公立医院所有品种的共同变化、(b) 集采品种在所有医院的共同变化。δ 不等于任何一组的前后差：公立·集采的前后差 −23 万元里混着 γ2 + γ12 + γ23 + δ 四项。
- **图形直觉**：画四组均值线（公立·集采、公立·非集采、民营·集采、民营·非集采），DDD 就是「两条实线之间斜率差」减「两条虚线之间斜率差」。期望 8 组均值（噪声平均掉后）：

| 单元格 | 政策前 | 政策后 | 前后差 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 公立 · 集采 | 135 | 112 | −23 |
| 公立 · 非集采 | 110 | 99 | −11 |
| 民营 · 集采 | 120 | 111 | −9 |
| 民营 · 非集采 | 100 | 95 | −5 |

品种 DID（公立切片）＝ −23 − (−11) ＝ −12（把 δ = −8 与 γ23 = −4 混在一起）；品种 DID（民营切片）＝ −9 − (−5) ＝ −4（纯 γ23）；DDD ＝ −12 − (−4) ＝ −8，正好剔掉 γ23。镜像读法：医院 DID（集采切片）＝ −23 − (−9) ＝ −14（混着 γ12 = −6）；医院 DID（非集采切片）＝ −11 − (−5) ＝ −6；DDD ＝ −14 − (−6) ＝ −8。
- **什么时候用 DDD 而不是两个 DID**：两个维度的平行趋势都明显不可信、但可论证「威胁不随第三维度变化」时，用 DDD；只要某一维平行趋势（或偏误同质性）明显更可信，就优先用简单 DID——假设更少、效力更高、更好解释。第三维度必须分层清晰、尽量外生、8 个单元格样本均衡。

**代码**：

```stata
* 图形直觉：四组均值线（先平均到 8 个单元格）
preserve
collapse (mean) y, by(treated post group)
twoway (connected y post if treated==1 & group==1, sort) ///
       (connected y post if treated==1 & group==0, sort) ///
       (connected y post if treated==0 & group==1, sort) ///
       (connected y post if treated==0 & group==0, sort), ///
       legend(order(1 "公立·集采" 2 "公立·非集采" 3 "民营·集采" 4 "民营·非集采")) ///
       xtitle("post（0 政策前 / 1 政策后）") ytitle("月均药品费用（万元）")
restore
```

```r
# 图形直觉：四组均值线（两条 DID 线的斜率差之差 = DDD）
cell <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post + group, data = dat, FUN = mean)
plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = range(cell$y),
     xlab = "post（0 政策前 / 1 政策后）", ylab = "月均药品费用 y（万元）",
     main = "四组均值线：DDD = 实线斜率差 - 虚线斜率差")
lines(y ~ post, data = cell, subset = treated == 1 & group == 1, type = "b", col = "red",  lty = 1)
lines(y ~ post, data = cell, subset = treated == 1 & group == 0, type = "b", col = "blue", lty = 1)
lines(y ~ post, data = cell, subset = treated == 0 & group == 1, type = "b", col = "red",  lty = 2)
lines(y ~ post, data = cell, subset = treated == 0 & group == 0, type = "b", col = "blue", lty = 2)
legend("topright", c("公立·集采", "公立·非集采", "民营·集采", "民营·非集采"),
       col = c("red", "blue", "red", "blue"), lty = c(1, 1, 2, 2), bty = "n")
```

### 第 2 步：模型设定与估计（Stata / R 对应）

**方法**：饱和模型（所有主效应 + 全部两两交互 + 三重交互）：

Y = γ0 + γ1·treated + γ2·post + γ3·group + γ12·(treated×post) + γ13·(treated×group) + γ23·(post×group) + δ·(treated×post×group) + ε

逐项解释（基组 = 民营 × 政策前 × 非集采品种）：

- γ1（treated）：处理组与对照组的固定水平差（公立 vs 民营，品种平均）；
- γ2（post）：政策前后全体平均变化（时间主效应）；
- γ3（group）：第三维度两切片的固定差（集采 vs 非集采品种）；
- γ12（treated×post）：**偏误 1**——处理组特有趋势（公立医院所有品种的共同变化）；
- γ13（treated×group）：处理组内品种结构的固定差异（公立医院更依赖集采品种）；
- γ23（post×group）：**偏误 2**——第三维度特有趋势（集采品种在所有医院的共同变化）；
- δ（treated×post×group）：三重交互 = **政策净效应**，本 Skill 的核心系数。

**两两交互项一个都不能漏**：漏掉 γ12 或 γ23，δ 会把偏误吞进去；漏掉主效应则模型不饱和。

**Stata**：

- `i.treated##i.post##i.group` 中 `##` =「主效应 + 交互」，`#` =「仅交互」。三者连写展开为 7 项：`i.treated`、`i.post`、`i.group`（3 个主效应）＋ `i.treated#i.post`、`i.treated#i.group`、`i.post#i.group`（3 个两两交互）＋ `i.treated#i.post#i.group`（1 个三重交互）。
- 模型 A：`reg y i.treated##i.post##i.group, vce(cluster id)`（pooled OLS + 医院聚类稳健标准误）。
- 模型 B：`reghdfe y i.treated##i.post##i.group, absorb(id time) vce(cluster id)`。`absorb(id)` 吸收医院固定效应后 `treated` 主效应与 id 共线、`absorb(time)` 吸收时间固定效应后 `post` 主效应与 time 共线，这两个主效应会被 reghdfe 自动剔除并在输出中标注（collinearity）；其余交互项仍可估，δ 与模型 A 相同（饱和交互设定下等价）。若希望保留全部主效应，用模型 A 或不吸收 time。
- 以 help reghdfe 为准。

**R（fixest）**：

- `feols(y ~ treated*post*group | id + time, cluster = ~id)`。fixest 里 `*` 展开为主效应 + 全部交互（对应 Stata 的 `##`），`:` 只写单个交互（对应 Stata 的 `#`）；`(treated + post + group)^3` 也展开为全部 7 项。`|` 后为固定效应，`cluster = ~id` 为聚类稳健标准误。
- 变量保持 0/1 数值型时，系数 `treated:post:group` 就是 δ；若改用 factor，fixest 会生成水平虚拟变量（需确认参照水平），因此建议保持 0/1 数值型。吸收 id、time 后 treated、post 因共线被自动移除（输出会提示 collinearity）。以 fixest 帮助文档为准。

**代码**：

```stata
* ---------- 模型 A：pooled OLS + 医院聚类稳健标准误 ----------
reg y i.treated##i.post##i.group, vce(cluster id)
est store ddd_ols

* ---------- 模型 B：医院 + 时间固定效应（reghdfe） ----------
reghdfe y i.treated##i.post##i.group, absorb(id time) vce(cluster id)
est store ddd_fe
* 说明：treated、post 主效应被吸收（与 id / time 固定效应共线，输出中标注）；
*       两两交互与三重交互仍可估，δ 与模型 A 相同
```

```r
library(fixest)

# 模型 A：pooled OLS + 医院聚类稳健标准误（不吸收固定效应）
m_ols <- feols(y ~ treated*post*group, cluster = ~id, data = dat)
summary(m_ols)

# 模型 B：医院 + 时间固定效应（treated、post 因共线被自动移除）
m_fe <- feols(y ~ treated*post*group | id + time, cluster = ~id, data = dat)
summary(m_fe)

# 三重交互系数 δ（fixest 中交互用 ":" 连接，对应 Stata 的 #）
coef(m_fe)["treated:post:group"]
```

### 第 3 步：核心系数 δ 的解读与分解验证

**方法**：

- **δ 的边际含义（两种双重差分之差）**：
  δ ＝ [E(Y|公立,集采,后) − E(Y|公立,集采,前) − E(Y|公立,非集采,后) + E(Y|公立,非集采,前)] − [民营对应项] ＝ **品种 DID（公立切片）− 品种 DID（民营切片）**；镜像等价于 **医院 DID（集采切片）− 医院 DID（非集采切片）**。
- **验证性分解表**：先跑两个 2×2 DID（第三维度各取一个切片），再跑完整 DDD，展示「DDD ＝ DID1 − DID2」。用本模拟数据：DID1（品种|公立）≈ −12、DID2（品种|民营）≈ −4、DDD ≈ −12 − (−4) ＝ −8 ＝ 主回归三重交互系数；镜像分解 −14 − (−6) ＝ −8。若分解表与三重交互系数对不上，先查模型设定（漏交互项、参照组、编码）而不是查数据。
- **报告口径**：δ 的单位与 y 一致（本例为「万元/月」）；若 y 取对数，δ ≈ 半弹性（百分点的近似）。分解表同时暴露两个偏误的方向与大小（本例：−6 与 −4，均使单维 DID 高估政策效果）。

**代码**：

```stata
* ---------- 3.1 两个 2×2 DID（品种类型 DID，在公立/民营切片上） ----------
reg y i.post##i.group if treated == 1, vce(cluster id)
local did1 = _b[1.post#1.group]          // 期望 ≈ -12（= γ23 + δ）
reg y i.post##i.group if treated == 0, vce(cluster id)
local did2 = _b[1.post#1.group]          // 期望 ≈ -4（= γ23）

* ---------- 3.2 分解：DDD = DID1 - DID2 ----------
display "DID1(品种|公立) = " %5.2f `did1'
display "DID2(品种|民营) = " %5.2f `did2'
display "DDD = DID1 - DID2 = " %5.2f (`did1' - `did2')

* ---------- 3.3 镜像分解（医院类型 DID，在集采/非集采切片上） ----------
reg y i.treated##i.post if group == 1, vce(cluster id)
local did1b = _b[1.treated#1.post]       // 期望 ≈ -14（= γ12 + δ）
reg y i.treated##i.post if group == 0, vce(cluster id)
local did2b = _b[1.treated#1.post]       // 期望 ≈ -6（= γ12）
display "镜像分解：DID(医院|集采) - DID(医院|非集采) = " %5.2f (`did1b' - `did2b')

* ---------- 3.4 与主回归三重交互系数对照（期望 ≈ -8） ----------
reg y i.treated##i.post##i.group, vce(cluster id)
display "主回归三重交互系数 δ = " %5.2f _b[1.treated#1.post#1.group]
```

```r
# 3.1 两个 2×2 DID（品种类型 DID 在公立/民营切片上）
did1 <- coef(feols(y ~ post*group | id, cluster = ~id, data = dat[dat$treated == 1, ]))["post:group"]
did2 <- coef(feols(y ~ post*group | id, cluster = ~id, data = dat[dat$treated == 0, ]))["post:group"]
c(DID1 = unname(did1), DID2 = unname(did2), DDD = unname(did1 - did2))
# 期望：DID1 ≈ -12，DID2 ≈ -4，DDD ≈ -8 = δ

# 3.2 镜像分解（医院类型 DID 在集采/非集采切片上），期望 ≈ -8
d1 <- coef(feols(y ~ treated*post | id, cluster = ~id, data = dat[dat$group == 1, ]))["treated:post"]
d2 <- coef(feols(y ~ treated*post | id, cluster = ~id, data = dat[dat$group == 0, ]))["treated:post"]
unname(d1 - d2)

# 3.3 与主回归三重交互系数对照（期望 ≈ -8）
coef(m_fe)["treated:post:group"]
```
